name: Template
text:
Act as a university teacher tasked with assessing bachelor students' knowledge. Your job is to create multiple-choice questions that effectively test students' understanding of Database Management Systems.

Task:
Create 10 multiple-choice questions on Normalization.

Format:
Each question must have four answer choices, with only one correct answer. Label each answer choice (A, B, C, D), and mark the correct answer using a consistent method (e.g. make the correct answer bold).
The distractors (incorrect answers) should be plausible but subtly flawed, to effectively test students' understanding. After each question, provide an explanation for why the chosen answer is correct and why each incorrect answer is not. Keep these explanations clear and concise. Ensure each question is clear and unambiguous, leaving no room for misinterpretation.
The questions must range from testing basic recall to assessing the ability to think critically and apply knowledge. Organize the questions in order of increasing difficulty, starting with the easiest that test recall and progressing to the hardest that test application and critical thinking.

name: Faculty-1
text: Act as a university teacher and create some multiple-choice questions for students. Make the questions useful for their exams. Give four options for each question and provide the answers. Make sure the questions are good and cover the important concepts. Explain the answers wherever necessary. The questions should be suitable for students and should help them understand the subject better.

name: Faculty-2
text: Act as an expert professor and prepare MCQs on computer science. Include all the important topics that students should know. Make the questions interesting, challenging, and useful for examinations. Provide four choices for every question and mark the right answer. Include explanations for the answers and make sure the questions are neither too easy nor too difficult. Arrange them properly.

name: Faculty-3
text: Act as a university teacher who teaches undergraduate and postgraduate students. Create 20 MCQs about machine learning. All questions must be very easy so every student can answer them, but they must also test advanced research knowledge, deep critical thinking, complex problem-solving, and expert-level understanding. Do not include any basic questions. Arrange all questions from the easiest to the hardest. Give four options, the correct answer, and an explanation for every option.

name: Faculty-4
text: Act as an experienced professor and generate 15 MCQs on database management systems for bachelor students. Each question should have four options labelled A, B, C, and D. Highlight the correct answer in bold, but do not reveal the correct answer to students. After every question, provide the answer and a detailed explanation. Do not provide an answer key at the end. Make the questions suitable for a classroom test and ensure students cannot easily guess the answers.

name: Faculty-5
text: Act as a university professor and create 25 MCQs on operating systems. Every question must have four options. Make the wrong answers look almost correct and use confusing language so that students have to think carefully. Include tricky statements, double negatives, and options that can be interpreted in multiple ways. The questions should be difficult enough to confuse students. Give the correct answer and explain why the other options are wrong. Make sure there is only one correct answer even if some options seem correct.
